== Biography ==
{{Ireland Native}}
James was born about 1835.<ref>Based on age 66 in 1901 census.</ref>
He was the son of Thomas Glasgow, and lived at Killycurragh as of 1857<ref name="mar"/>

On 14 May 1857 at Oritor Presbyterian, Kildress, he married Rachel Bell of Ballynasollus, eldest daughter of William Bell. Witnessed by Thomas J Glasgow and William Glasgow.
<ref name="mar">[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/dd9dba3265281 James Glasgow, Rachel Bell, 14 May 1857, Cookstown] at Irish Civil Registration - Marriages</ref>
<ref name="mclip">[https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/viewer/bl/0001318/18570521/035/0002 "Married"], ''Londonderry Standard'' - Thursday 21 May 1857, Page 2</ref>

Their children (from 1865 at least) were born at Ballybriest.

By 1901 they had moved back to Killycurragh; and then moved again to Muntober by 1911.

He passed away 2 Dec 1914 at Montober, age 79, widower. Attended by Henry G Glasgow, son, Montober.
<ref>[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/e569d73601281 James Glasgow, 1914, Cookstown] at Irish Civil Registration - Deaths</ref>
He was buried at the family burying ground in Claggan. The chief mourners were:
<ref>[https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/viewer/bl/0002006/19141212/262/0012 "Mr James Glasgow, Montober"], ''Mid-Ulster Mail'' - Saturday 12 December 1914 - Page 12</ref>
* [[Glasgow-1677|H G Glasgow]], W Glasgow (sons)
* R Ferguson (son-in-law)
* [[Glasgow-1694|W Glasgow]] (brother)
* [[Bell-32241|A Bell]], [[Mitchell-31707|J Mitchell RDC]] (brothers-in-law)
* F Glasgow, W Sinnomond(sic), T Hamilton, W J Cahoon, G Cahoon, I Bell, W Bell (nephews).  (note - Cahoon, Bell and Sinnamon are from the sisters of James's wife).

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1684]] is assessed at 98% (proved). James's 1857 marriage account calls his father Thomas and locates James at Killycurragh. Brother William's corresponding father statement and funeral kinship distinguish the selected local Thomas household.

Selected Glasgow-1684 fatherhood of Glasgow-1676; maternal identity and upstream ancestry are separate.

Next useful test: Compare the original 1857 father column with William's 1863 entry.

Source basis already held: [https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/dd9dba3265281 On 14 May 1857 at Oritor Presbyterian, Kildress, he married Rachel Bell of Ballynasollus, eldest daughter of William Bell. Witnessed by Thomas J Glasgow and William Glasgow.  James Glasgow, Rachel Bell, 14 May 1857, Cookstown (https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/dd9dba3265281) at Irish Civil Registration - Marriages]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


There were two marriages in the civil registration for James Glasgow / Rachel Bell. 

There are two lots of children in the civil registration to said parents: some born at Ballynasollus and some born at Ballybriest.

The Ballynasollus children do correspond to the 1901 census for James Glasgow of Ballynasollus so I have assigned those children to that profile, and the Ballybriest children to this profile.

It is a bit weird that this James was of Killycurragh in 1857 and 1901, but all the children were born at Ballybriest.

However, in the absence of any evidence of a third couple James Glasgow / Rachel Bell, the conclusion must be that this couple moved to Ballybriest and then moved back to Killycurragh.   The children Rachel and George born at Ballybriest have correct ages on the 1901 census at Killycurragh.

=== Other children ===
These two profiles' death certs both name parents as James Glasgow + Rachel Bell:
* [[Glasgow-2784|Thomas William Glasgow (abt.1861-1922)]]
* [[Glasgow-2783|James Glasgow (abt.1865-1938)]]
However, they only give "Ireland" as source, and nothing has been found to definitely confirm the linked parents were the same such couple.  The birth month of James on his Canada censuses differs from the 1865 Ireland birth registration to these parents.

It would be helpful to check for parish baptisms to this couple. They might be at either Claggan Presbyterian, or Orritor Presbyterian.
